title: Tomas Rell and the Road's Pattern

paragraphs.text: Tomas Rell keeps polishing the same cup instead of setting it away. The common room talks in low pockets around him, every road rumor arriving before the door fully shuts.
He wants to be useful, but only as far as fear will let him. When the broken caravan comes up, his eyes move toward the hearth before he answers.
Ordinary bandits, Tomas says, have habits. What has been happening on the Grey Road has a pattern he does not like and cannot comfortably name.

passive_social_insight.label: Tomas is guarding the room against panic

on_success.text: Your read of anxious innkeepers catches the restraint in him: Tomas is not hiding a culprit. He is afraid that naming what he cannot prove will make fear do its own damage.

relationship_writes.reason: The player recognizes that Tomas is careful rather than evasive.

result.text: Tomas sets the cup down at last. "Bandits take what they can and run. This is not that. Sometimes the violence is clean. Sometimes it stops dead, like someone turned them toward another thought."
result.summary: Tomas says the Grey Road attacks do not behave like ordinary banditry.

knowledge_grants.title: Pattern of Attacks
knowledge_grants.summary: Tomas has been comparing road reports and believes the attacks are inconsistent with ordinary banditry.

relationship_writes.reason: Tomas can answer safely when asked for a pattern rather than certainty.

result.text: He nods toward the quieter side of the room. "One woman made it. Elin Harrow. Be patient if you speak to her; memory has not been kind."
result.summary: Tomas points toward Elin Harrow, a survivor of the Grey Road attack.

result.text: "Fewer wagons. Shorter stops. People watching the door before they ask for rooms." Tomas glances across the common room. "Fear travels faster than horses when it has a road to itself."
result.summary: Tomas has seen fewer travelers and more fear moving through the inn.

relationship_writes.reason: Ordinary inn details keep the conversation grounded.

clarifying_questions.label: What do you mean by the road's temper?

result.text: "Roads have moods when you hear enough people come off them," Tomas says. "This one has gone quiet in the wrong places."
result.summary: Tomas describes the Grey Road's change as a practical innkeeper's instinct, not proof.
